issues.display_title: Issue #1176: fix(dashboard): closing a menu modal by clicking outside it opens the project
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported in #1174 (37 s screen recording, production): on the dashboard, open a published project's … menu → Share, then close the Share modal by clicking the dimmed area outside it. The modal closes and the project opens in the editor straight away ("Loading project…"). The same happens on the Blue Line Map dashboard ("Loading Blue Line Map…" → Blue Line Map editor). Closing the modal must leave the user on the dashboard.

Closing with the × button or Escape does not navigate; only a click on the backdrop does.

Root cause

The row/tile … menu (ActionsMenu) mounts its modals inside the clickable project card, and the card opens the project on click:

  • src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx:358 (ProjectTile) and :436 (ProjectRow): onClick={open} → router.push(href).

The modals are portaled out of the card in the DOM, but React synthetic events still bubble up the component tree. PreviewModal already knows this and stops clicks on the popup (src/components/preview/PreviewModal.tsx:51), but not on its backdrop (:45):

<Dialog.Backdrop className="fixed inset-0 z-[100] …" />   // ← click bubbles to the card
<Dialog.Popup onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()} …>     // ← stopped

base-ui closes a modal dialog on an "intentional" outside press, i.e. on the click itself, and the target of that click is the backdrop. So one click closes the modal and then reaches the card's onClick.

Reproduced in a jsdom test (temporary, removed): row and tile × Share / Unpublish / Duplicate / Delete. A backdrop click closes the dialog and calls router.push, failing 8/8. With onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()} on the backdrop, the dialog still closes and router.push is not called, passing 8/8.

Affected

Every modal the … menu opens, on both dashboards (Workspace and Blue Line Map), from a row or a tile:

  • Share
  • Publish / Unpublish
  • Duplicate
  • Delete
  • the owner-only dialog

All of them are built on PreviewModal.

Scope

  1. Stop click propagation on the PreviewModal backdrop, next to the popup's existing guard. One place covers every modal above.
  2. No change to how the modal closes: a backdrop click, × and Escape all still close it.
  3. No change to the card's own click / Enter / Space behaviour.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dashboard → … → Share → click outside the modal: the modal closes and the dashboard stays.
  • Same on the Blue Line Map dashboard.
  • Same for Publish / Unpublish / Duplicate / Delete, from a row and from a tile.
  • Clicking the project card itself still opens the project.
  • A regression test fails if a backdrop click reaches the card.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Source: #1174

RESULT

video-1176-modal-click-outside.mp4

Released to main on 2026-10-07: PR #1177 → development 260618e5, release PR #1179 → main fa65019c. Deploy run 37566412555 succeeded. Live on map-thru.com.

Fix: src/components/preview/PreviewModal.tsx. The backdrop now stops click propagation, as the popup already did. The click that closes a modal from the dashboard's … menu no longer reaches the project card, so the editor no longer opens. One place covers every modal of that menu, on both dashboards:

  • Share
  • Publish / Unpublish
  • Duplicate
  • Delete
  • the owner-only dialog

The modal still closes on a click outside, on × and on Escape.

Tests: new src/components/dashboard/__tests__/ProjectMenuModalClose.test.tsx, 12 tests, run for a row and for a tile:

  • Share / Unpublish / Duplicate / Delete: a click outside closes the modal without navigating.
  • × does not navigate.
  • A click on the card itself still opens the project.

Without the fix, 8 of the 12 fail. pnpm test (2924), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked in a real browser with .playwright-mcp/demo/1176/check-backdrop.mjs (Chrome, read only: any navigation off the dashboard is aborted). Cases: Workspace Share, Workspace Duplicate, Blue Line Map Share. Results are passed checks out of 6.

Build Result
development before the fix 3/6: all three cases open the editor
This branch 6/6
Production after the deploy 6/6: the modal closes and the dashboard stays

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1176/video-1176-modal-click-outside.mp4, before and after in one take, on a scratch copy deleted afterwards.

Commit: 3e1e86c9

issues.display_title: Issue #1180: fix(map): the satellite tile proxy refuses real tile coordinates
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported in #1175 (67 s screen recording, production): picking Satellite turns the map black in the Blue Line Map editor and in the floor plan editor's Map tab. Street and 3D Building work.

Every satellite tile goes through MapThru's proxy GET /api/tiles/satellite/{z}/{x}/{y} (SATELLITE_STYLE in src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx). The proxy fails in production at every zoom, for two separate reasons. The satellite style replaces the street style, so with no tile the map shows only its empty background.

Cause 1 (this task): the proxy rejects real tile coordinates

src/app/api/tiles/satellite/[z]/[x]/[y]/route.ts:15:

const TILE_COORD = /^\d{1,3}$/;

This came in with the path-traversal fix a256f5be (2026-07-28). Tile x/y pass 999 from zoom ~11 up, so every street-level or building-level tile is refused before it is fetched. For example, Subang at z12 is x=3274 and Toronto at z18 is x=73262.

https://map-thru.com/api/tiles/satellite/12/3274/2122       → 400 {"error":"invalid tile coordinates"}
https://map-thru.com/api/tiles/satellite/18/209530/135891   → 400 {"error":"invalid tile coordinates"}

The existing test (src/app/api/tiles/__tests__/route.test.ts) only proxies 17/104/63, a coordinate no real map at z17 requests, so it stayed green.

Cause 2 (server, not this repo's code): the API cannot reach maps.gothru.co

https://map-thru.com/api/tiles/satellite/3/6/4 → 500
GET 192.168.1.226:7070/v1/tiles/satellite/3/6/4 → 500
  Get "https://maps.gothru.co/data/satelite/3/6/4": tls: failed to verify certificate:
  x509: certificate is valid for pfSense-5da105716e196, not maps.gothru.co

From the API host, maps.gothru.co loops back through the pfSense, which answers with its own certificate. The Go API reads the tile base from env NEXT_PUBLIC_SATELITE_SOURCE_DATA (default https://maps.gothru.co/data/satelite, src/action/v1/tiles/satellite.go). So the fix is server configuration, done by whoever runs the servers. Either:

  • point that env at the tile server's internal address, or
  • map maps.gothru.co to the internal address on 192.168.1.226.

Satellite only works again once both are fixed.

Cause 3 (found while building the demo): no imagery past z18

SATELLITE_STYLE in src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx sets no maxzoom on the raster source. MapLibre therefore asks for z19+ tiles at the building zooms the floor plan editor sits at.

The imagery stops at z18: maps.gothru.co's own satellite source declares maxzoom={18}. Past z18 the tile server answers 200 with a grey "Map data not yet available" tile. Subang: z18 18/209541/135853 has imagery, z19 19/419083/271706 is that grey tile.

Even with causes 1 and 2 fixed, the Map tab would show grey at building zoom. The fix is maxzoom: 18 on the source, so z18 is overzoomed.

Scope

  1. Accept every real tile coordinate: zoom up to two digits, and x/y anything from 0 to 2^z − 1.
  2. Keep the traversal guard: integers only, checked on every segment, nothing else goes upstream.
  3. Refuse x/y outside the zoom's tile grid without calling upstream.
  4. No change to the upstream URL, headers or caching.
  5. Satellite source maxzoom: 18, so building zooms overzoom the z18 imagery.

Acceptance criteria

  • /api/tiles/satellite/18/209530/135891 (and other real tiles at z ≥ 11) is proxied upstream, not refused with 400.
  • ../, non-numeric, exponent, negative and empty segments are still refused with 400 without calling upstream.
  • A coordinate outside the grid of its zoom (e.g. 2/4/0) is refused with 400.
  • Tests use real building-zoom coordinates.
  • At building zoom (z19+) the satellite map shows the z18 imagery scaled up, not grey "Map data not yet available" tiles.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.
  • After cause 2 is fixed on the server: Satellite shows imagery in the Blue Line Map editor and the floor plan editor's Map tab.

Source: #1175

RESULT

video-1180-satellite-tiles.mp4

Released to main on 2026-10-07:

  • PR #1181 → development 8c2942cf.
  • Release PR #1182 → main 644a349e.
  • Deploy run 37572280570 succeeded.

Fixed (code half):

  1. src/app/api/tiles/satellite/[z]/[x]/[y]/route.ts: the 3-digit cap is replaced by isTile(). Zoom can be up to two digits, and x and y must be integers below 2^z. The traversal guard holds (integers only, every segment checked). A coordinate outside the grid is refused without calling upstream.
  2. src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx: SATELLITE_STYLE sets maxzoom: 18, so building zooms overzoom the z18 imagery instead of asking for grey "Map data not yet available" z19+ tiles. This covers the Blue Line Map editor, the floor plan editor's Map tab, the preview and the floor image position modal.

Tests: src/app/api/tiles/__tests__/route.test.ts now has 15 tests and uses real tiles:

  • 0/0/0, Subang 12/3274/2122, Toronto 18/73262/95669, and the last tile of z22.
  • Out-of-grid x/y and a three-digit zoom are refused.
  • The existing traversal, non-numeric, exponent, negative and empty cases are kept.

Restoring the 3-digit cap fails 3 tests; dropping the grid bound fails 2. pnpm test (2933), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Production after the deploy:

Tile Before Now
12/3274/2122, 18/209541/135853 400 (refused by the proxy) 500 (forwarded; the API cannot reach maps.gothru.co)
2/4/0 (outside the grid) 500 400

Satellite is still black on production until cause 2 is fixed on the server. Either set env NEXT_PUBLIC_SATELITE_SOURCE_DATA on the Go API to the tile server's internal address, or map maps.gothru.co to that address on 192.168.1.226. #1175 stays open until then.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1180/video-1180-satellite-tiles.mp4 (98 s). Before and after in one take, against 1180/be-sim.mjs, which plays the API with cause 2 fixed, so only the FE differs:

  • development: the Blue Line Map editor is black at street zoom, every tile 400. At z10 the imagery appears.
  • This fix: imagery from z14 to z18 in the Blue Line Map editor, and at z20.8 in the floor plan editor's Map tab, on a scratch copy that was deleted afterwards.

Commits: 8a63dd70, e56920b5

issues.display_title: Issue #1183: fix(blue-line): tour lines are not drawn below zoom 14
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Found while verifying #1175 on production: a Blue Line Map's tour lines are not drawn at all below zoom 14, on the public map /m/{key} and in the Blue Line Map editor alike. This holds in Street, Satellite and 3D Building.

queryRenderedFeatures on blue-line-map-lines, published map "Subang" (/m/fPMEbGwq, 2 tours), production:

zoom 12 13 13.97 14 14.13
public /m 0 0 0 2 2
editor 0 0 0 2 2

At 1440×900 the editor fits Subang at z13.97, because the sidebar narrows the map. So it opens with no lines. At 1920 wide it fits at ≥14, so the lines show.

A project whose tours lie further apart fits at a lower zoom and shows no line at all.

Cause

tourFeatures (src/lib/blueLine/mapTours.ts) builds one MultiLineString per tour with one two-point part per segment: each [lng, lat, lng, lat] of the stored lines, i.e. one pano-to-pano hop of a few metres. Cigadung has 189 parts, Jalan Raya Pramuka 29.

MapLibre's GeoJSON source tiles the data with geojson-vt, which skips a line part shorter than the source tolerance (default 0.375) at that tile zoom. Below z14 every one of those metre-long parts is under it, so nothing is left to draw.

Checked client side on the production /m page by re-adding the same data as a test source:

source parts z12 z13 z14
as stored (tolerance 0.375) 29 + 189 0 0 2
tolerance: 0 29 + 189 2 2 2
contiguous segments merged 1 + 39 2 2 2

Subang's geometry is synthetic (3 m steps), but real Street View tours also space their panoramas a few metres apart, so they produce the same tiny parts.

Scope

  1. Draw the tour lines at every zoom the map can fit to, in the editor and on /m.
  2. Prefer fixing the shape at its source: merge contiguous segments (end of one = start of the next) into continuous lines in tourFeatures. It is shared by the editor, /m and the public GET /api/m/{key}/lines (#1171). That way maps.gothru.co's embed (gothru-maps-frontend#132) gets whole lines too.
  3. Segments that do not join stay separate parts. Nothing is dropped and nothing is bridged across a gap.
  4. If a short isolated run can still vanish when zoomed far out, also set tolerance: 0 on the tour source in TourLinesMap.
  5. No change to the stored blue_line_tours data or the Go API.

Acceptance criteria

  • /m/fPMEbGwq and the Subang editor draw both tours at z12, z13 and z14, at 1440×900.
  • The editor at 1440×900 opens with the tour lines visible, in Street and Satellite.
  • Clicking a line still selects or opens its tour, with mid intact on the merged features.
  • GET /api/m/{key}/lines returns merged lines with the same properties (mid, tourKey, name, panoramaCount) and the same bbox.
  • Unit tests: contiguous segments merge into one part, a gap starts a new part, and no coordinate is lost.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

video-1183-tour-lines-zoom.mp4

Released to main on 2026-10-07:

  • PR #1184 → development cd50af45.
  • Release PR #1185 → main f250498a.
  • Deploy run 37582220613 succeeded.

Fix: src/lib/blueLine/mapTours.ts. lineRuns() joins lines that meet into runs, where a line starts at the point where the one before it ends.

  • A gap or a branch starts a new run. Nothing is bridged and no line is lost.
  • Subang goes from 29 + 189 parts to 1 + 39, and both tours draw down to z9.
  • tolerance: 0 was tried and is not needed.
  • tourFeatures also feeds GET /api/m/{key}/lines, so maps.gothru.co's embed gets the runs with the same properties and bbox.
  • No change to stored data or the Go API.

Tests:

  • mapTours.test.ts: join, gap and branch cases, and every input line can be read back from the runs.
  • route.test.ts: the API serves runs, and the bbox is unchanged.
  • Mutation check: dropping the join fails 3 tests; joining across gaps fails 1.
  • pnpm test (2935), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Production, checked in real Chrome at 1440×900 with .playwright-mcp/demo/1183/check-lines-zoom.mjs (read only):

Check Before deploy After deploy
API serves runs 29 + 189 parts 1 + 39 parts
/m draws both tours at z12 and z13 0 tours 2 tours
Editor opens with both tours (z13.97) 0 tours 2 tours
Editor draws both tours at z12 and z13 0 tours 2 tours
A line takes the pointer at z13 no yes
Total 2/10 10/10

The maps.gothru.co embed re-checked after the deploy (1156/check-maps-embed.mjs): 8/8. Both tours are drawn, and a click opens the tour.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1183/video-1183-tour-lines-zoom.mp4 (64 s), before and after in one take with a zoom and "tours drawn" counter.

Commit: 9dfcd35a

issues.display_title: Issue #1186: feat(blue-line): edit a Blue Line Map's project information
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Requested in #1178: an Edit button on the Blue Line Map editor's Project Information card. It opens a modal to edit the project's name, address, latitude and longitude, with a map preview.

Today

  • The Project Information card (src/components/blue-line/map/BlueLineMapSidebar.tsx) only shows the name, address and coordinates. Nothing edits them after the project is created.
  • The form already exists: ProjectLocationForm + useProjectLocationForm(initial) (src/components/projects/ProjectLocationForm.tsx). It has the name, an address search, latitude/longitude and a map with the project pin in the middle. It is used by Create a Blue Line Map project, Create New Empty Project, and Clone as 3D Project, which opens it prefilled.
  • updateProject and the API's PATCH /v1/projects/:id already take name, locationAddress, locationLat and locationLng. No Go API change is needed.

Scope

  1. An Edit button on the Project Information card.
  2. A modal built on ProjectLocationForm, prefilled with the project's name, address and coordinates.
  3. Save in the modal stores the change right away with updateProject. It is separate from the editor's Save, which stores the tours. Cancel or closing the modal changes nothing.
  4. After a save, the editor shows the new values without a reload: the card, the name in the nav, and the location the map opens at when the project has no tours.
  5. A failed save keeps the modal open with the error.

Acceptance criteria

  • The card has an Edit button that opens the modal with the current values.
  • The name, address, latitude and longitude can be changed; the map preview follows the coordinates.
  • Save is disabled while the form is invalid (empty name, coordinates out of range) or saving.
  • After Save, the card shows the new values and a reload keeps them.
  • Cancel and closing the modal leave the project unchanged.
  • A failed save shows the error and keeps what was typed.
  • Tours that are not saved yet stay unsaved and untouched.

Notes

  • Publishing stores no snapshot, so on a published project the new name and location are live at /m/{key} right away.
  • FE only: no Go API, env or dependency change.

RESULT

video-1186-edit-project-info.mp4

Released to main in 26f137b4 (release PR #1188). The feature came in through PR #1187, merged to development as 4abd9b4c; the feature commit is b90eece4.

The Project Information card in the Blue Line Map editor has an Edit button. It opens "Edit project information", which uses New Project's form (ProjectLocationForm) filled with the project's name, address, latitude and longitude, beside the map preview.

  • Save Changes stores them at once with updateProject, separate from the editor's Save, which stores the tours.
  • Cancel or closing the modal changes nothing.
  • After a save, the card and the Clone defaults show the new values without a reload. A project without tours flies the map to its new location.
  • Tours that are not saved yet stay unsaved.
  • An emptied address is sent as "", so it is cleared.
  • A failed save keeps the modal open, with the reason and what was typed.

One correction to the scope above: the editor's nav does not show the project name, so nothing there changes.

Files

  • src/components/blue-line/map/BlueLineMapProjectInfoModal.tsx (new)
  • src/components/blue-line/map/BlueLineMapSidebar.tsx: the Edit button.
  • src/components/blue-line/map/BlueLineMapEditor.tsx: the project info is held in state.
  • Tests: BlueLineMapProjectInfoModal.test.tsx (8), BlueLineMapEditor.test.tsx (+5), BlueLineMapSidebar.test.tsx (+1).

There is no Go API change: PATCH /v1/projects/:id already takes these fields.

Checked

  • pnpm test (2949), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.
  • Real Chrome: 16/16 on a scratch Blue Line Map project, created and deleted through the API.
  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1186/video-1186-edit-project-info.mp4.

Seen, not changed here

  • Typing coordinates key by key makes this form's map preview drift out to about z9: each keystroke starts a new flyTo that cuts the last one. New Project does the same.
  • The address search sometimes returns only a plus code.
